Glance at a Bayesian discount prior fit

Source: R/tidiers.R
glance.Rd

Return sample sizes, retained draw counts, and historical discount weights in a one-row tibble. These methods also work with broom::glance().

Usage

glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bdpbinomial'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bdpnormal'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bdplm'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bdpsurvival'
glance(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A fitted bdpbinomial, bdpnormal, bdplm, or bdpsurvival object. Fits from bdplogit() use class bdplm.

...

The table-formatting argument gof_map and coefficient-summary arguments exponentiate, effects, and time are accepted but do not affect model-level summaries. This allows modelsummary to forward them to both tidy() and glance(). Other arguments produce an error.

Value

A one-row tibble containing:

nobs

Number of current participants included in the analysis, summed across arms.

n.historical

Number of historical participants included in the analysis, summed across arms. Historical-only controls are counted here, not in nobs. An absent source contributes zero. These are unweighted counts, not effective sample sizes.

n.draws

Number of retained outcome posterior draws, counted from the saved draws rather than the requested simulation size. This is not a simulation effective sample size.

alpha.treatment, alpha.control

Median stored historical discount weight for each arm. A prescribed or estimated fixed weight is returned unchanged. NA indicates that a weight is not defined, including historical-only controls and absent arms or historical sources.

n.event, n.event.historical

For survival fits only, numbers of observed events among current and historical participants, respectively.

Details

Survival sample sizes and event counts use the saved participant records, not the rows created by splitting follow-up into hazard intervals. For older survival fits without participant records, these counts are NA; refit to obtain them. The columns and their order are fixed within each fitted class. No likelihood criteria, convergence diagnostics, or posterior comparison probabilities are supplied.

See also

tidy

Author

Graeme L. Hickey

Examples

set.seed(42)
fit <- bdpnormal(mu_t = 3, sigma_t = 2, N_t = 40,
  mu0_t = 2.8, sigma0_t = 2, N0_t = 60,
  method = "fixed", number_mcmc = 1000)
glance(fit)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>    nobs n.historical n.draws alpha.treatment alpha.control
#>   <dbl>        <dbl>   <dbl>           <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1    40           60    1000           0.578            NA
